reviews.text: Great fun, challenging as hell (or maybe I just suck)

I’m not sure how to feel about this game. It’s clear that a lot of work has gone into its development, but that work feels unfocused. Put simply, this game doesn't know what it wants to be. It feels almost like a mix between a roguelite and a stealth game but doesn’t do either particularly well. For instance, you can hang on ledges and peek over, which would be very useful in a stealth game but doesn’t have much use in a roguelite. On the other hand each stage has a timer that rewards you with new unlockables, a feature more at home in a roguelite than a stealth game. Other mechanics like backstabbing, weapon aiming and picking up objects and throwing them also feel like they would lend themselves more to stealth gameplay. It’s unclear if the game wants you to go fast and clear stages quickly or take your time and think tactically. The hazards in each area share this same flaw. Traps are far too hard to see and do too much damage for how difficult they are to avoid. This is especially prevalent in low light levels where you will frequently walk into traps that are simply impossible to see. Lanterns explode when damaged and throw fire everywhere, which is an interesting mechanic except for the fact that the fire is extremely hard to avoid and shreds your health far too quickly. The screen blur when poisoned is frankly obnoxious rather than threatening unless you are attempting to platform. Traps being motion sensitive and can be triggered with weapons is another mechanic that would be more interesting in a stealth game. The gas and lava level hazards add an interesting bit of stress to stages, however this is somewhat marred by the movement mechanics. The movement feels inconsistent and unsatisfying in Aura of Worlds. The dodge roll is pretty much useless, being both too slow and too short range. Wall climbing is really awkward because you can can jump once off a wall, but on low walls you will launch upwards to the ledge. This makes it feel inconsistent and unclear how far upwards you can easily climb in a pinch, most obviously in the rising lava stages. The movement abilities are interesting to experiment with but because both the levels and player equipment are randomly generated none of those abilities can be used in truly unique and interesting ways. The most they’re used for is getting around slightly easier and maybe getting an extra chest or two. On the plus side, the art is nice and the environments are interesting to look at. However, the enemy design and, by extension, the entire games aesthetic clashes in places. For the most part it has a fantasy vibe to it with slimes and bats and skeleton enemies but then in other places there are turrets and drones. Level hazards vary from automatic and motion activated arrows to lasers and gravity lifts. It’s a very strange mix of ideas and feels very unfocused from an art design perspective. Overall, I can’t really recommend the game in its current state. I hope it improves before release and finds a more concrete identity, but at the moment it’s a fairly weak roguelite.

[h1]Introduction[/h1] This is one of the few “overhauled” reviews I intend to re-evaluate, as the game in question has improved substantially since my initial impressions. It wouldn’t have been fair to just post a disclaimer or only a few added words here and there. We’re doing this the right way, as always. While I’m not exactly a glutton for digital punishment, I won’t deny the appeal which a rogue-like title can cast upon my daily gaming-related activities. The need for an extra challenge from a platforming subgenre that is inherently regarded as anything but child’s play, if you will. In fact, Aura of Worlds describes itself as a “roguelite” focusing on creative tactics and it does hit most of its intended targets once you get the hang of it. As the Steam debut for developer/publisher Cognitive Forge, the Early Access label suits it fine as it passed over a year since its release and following updates which chiseled the gameplay along with the narrative. [h1]Story [/h1] Indeed, a storyline is finally emerging in Aura of Worlds’ case. I know that given its current state and its pricing, I shouldn’t have expected anything near the territory of Dead Cells, Sundered or Hollow Knight since these cost more than double, to begin with. But I can at least compare it to the similarly priced and more recent Rift Keeper which also makes a minimal effort to convey a story along those lengthy dungeon/cave treks you embark upon. Aura of Worlds offers some context right in its intro video and the tutorial section further goes into detail acreoss its two levels covering the obvious basics. The irony that it doesn’t actually prepare you for the game itself, was to be expected. It’s meant to be tough-as-nails without necessarily having the charm of a full-fledged Metroidvania representative. The recently added Easy Mode featuring reduced XP yields along with fewer foes, ensures that even game reviewers can now proceed without significant delays. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1849696450 What more can we say about the narrative thread? It’s better than a static screen with some writing on it, even though it still has a hard time establishing an atmosphere. A step in the right direction, at least. I had to gather more details from a very unlikely source: the game’s Steam Achievements. You see, Aura of Worlds at least bears some resemblance towards a frame story. The titular Worlds are distinct from each other, so we can’t discuss continuity either. Grotto of Guidance is the first scenario you shall visit and invariably perish within it at least several times on the Normal or higher difficulties. The other two environments currently available are, Gnarled Gardens and Celestial Temple. From the level selection screen, you can see a few others greyed out as “work in progress”. Fingers crossed. The stages are filled to the brim with traps and foes, yet the boss fights are usually the final nails in the coffin of our nameless hero. [h1]Graphics[/h1] I couldn’t find plenty of intel on this title’s graphics engine, other than it being a “strain” of OpenGL. It’s certainly not Unity since it gave me a lot of headaches when I tried to capture even a few screenshots, like I do with all my Steam games. All that remains in the past, however. True to their word, the dev team worked hard at improving support for the Steam Overlay. I’m pleased to say that they even went above “the call of duty” by providing a HUDless option for both hardcore players and screenshots nutcases such as yours truly. There are no more crashes to report and images are captured and linked to Steam profiles, without further issues. Character customization for cloaks, arsenal and even skin tone, are just icing on the cake at this point. [h1]Audio[/h1] It would have been truly ironic if Aura of Worlds had any voice acting, considering the lack of a convincing storyline so far. But no, audio assets are limited to a repetitive soundtrack which I ended up muting and listening to my own playlists instead. You can’t have them all and this isn’t really a deal breaker even if there won’t be further changes to the OST. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1763609550 [h1]Gameplay[/h1] Aura of Worlds sure is lacking in some ragards but it will deliver its gameplay just as it’s being advertised. When you can die multiple times just from a game’s tutorial, you know that you’re only about to witness more digital torture in the subsequent levels. These titular Wolrds are are divided into over a dozen stages each. Randomly-generated maps filled with traps and bosses, during which you’ll certainly perish more than a few times. It certainly doesn’t help that health potions are hard to come by, while some lootable chests are in fact traps as well. Pretty much the entire environment will try to murder you as a few stages contain a so-called “polen cloud” which is essentially a poisonous gas that will rapidly descend and fill those caves, indiscriminately killing rogue protagonists and foes alike. Predictable patterns for the enemies shouldn’t be fully trusted as you won’t have an infinite amount of time at your disposal, to simply observe before swiftly striking. What could make these already hard conditions, considerably worse? Well, there’s also a timer on each stage. You dwell too much in one place and you’ll get “visited” by an immortal boss called “The Hunter”. You can use this giant floating skull as an incentive to find the stage exit sooner, but take my advice and keep a close eye on that timer. No hidden treasure is worth THAT much hassle. You could try the lowest difficulty setting now. I did and no more timers or immortals to worry about. The crossbow was my favorite offensive choice and while it takes some practice before you can eliminate most threats from afar, I like how gravity is simulated in the decreased damage and range of those bolts. Between certain stages, there’s also an in-game store where you can purchase power-ups and items with the coins you have plundered previously. Further more offensive choices have been added recently. It’s Hammertime! https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1849696581 [h1]Verdict[/h1] I’m rarely surprised by a game’s updates, since most of them don’t really add more content unless we’re talking of a DLC format. Aura of Worlds is no longer an excruciating experience in which you either adapt or quit. It may still be random to a fault, but the gameplay’s complexity remains consistent and may prove a worthy challenge for noobs and genre veterans alike. It’s worth a purchase especially during a Steam Sale, but you probably won’t regret paying the full price if you’re perfectly aware of what you going to face head-on. This title shan't hold hands while dishing its own brand of justice upon unsuspecting rogues. No cutting corners this time around. Just git gud, scrub! [h1]Strong Points[/h1] + Steam Achievements. + Gameplay features adequate diversity. + Difficulty enhanced by random factor and permadeath. + Supportive developer, constantly improving the project. [h1]Weak Points[/h1] - Storyline still needs further context. - No Steam Trading Cards yet. [b]Rating 75/100[/b] [quote]This review was submitted for [url=http://steamcommunity.com/groups/ImperialReviews]Imperial Reviews[/url] through the generous contribution of the game’s developer. Following my [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/25802515-Imperial-Reviews/]Curator Page[/url], will help me keep publishing new reviews as soon as I can. I appreciate your support![/quote]

**EDIT**: I may have been a bit too rude when writing my review - maybe stepped over a line, and I apologise for that. I'll leave up my original review, because erasing the past is a bad idea - instead I'd rather learn from it. HOWEVER I do think the way the developer handled my criticism, by contacting me over facebook and such, also crossed a line. When you receive a bad review, even a painful one, that is not the best way to handle it. Sometimes, you just need to let it go. **Original**: So what can I say about Aura of Worlds? * Art, though occasionally good, was extremely mismatched. * Music was passable. * Controls were difficult, like holding an eel. * Enemies had no strategy to defeating them, despite the complex item system. * World generation was meh, and in some cases actively detrimental. * The tutorial was completely superfluous due to a simple splash screen before the main game begins. * The hub world was also unnecessary. * HUD is too small, can't see it when focusing on the character. * No story, which is fine, but there was as splash screen with story, so I figured it would play a bigger part. * Not all stalactites are traps. * Not all items are traps, and it's not clear which ones until you get close. On the whole, after an hour of playing it, the only fun I had was when I saw two traps crush two enemies in succession - I didn't have a hand in that at all. I picked this up because I'd heard about it through the grape vine, and it really is as bad as they say. It's a great example of what not to do when designing a game. I'm a gamedev myself, and I'd be ashamed to put out a game this bad. Yeah, I'd say give this one a miss, unless you're deliberately looking for punishment. Which might be your thing, IDK.

一款横版随机生成地图的银河城肉鸽动作游戏。 与其去和死亡细胞比，倒不如说更像spelunky类的游戏。 可以算得上我玩过的体验最棒的一款类spelunky游戏，包括原版。 优点： +令人上头的魔性。 +操作很流畅。 +确实能营造每局不同体验的随机性。 +精准控制在好像能过又就是差一点的边缘反复摩擦的难度。 +不少去随机要素使得并不会太依赖运气。 +远程武器没有子弹限制真的是好文明！ 缺点： -手柄操作怎么设置都怪怪的。 建议给手柄加上 “禁止下键翻滚” “全自动锁定敌人” 和 “勾爪可用左摇杆/方向键控制方向” 3个选项。

横板动作游戏，说实话，我玩的并不是太多，印象最深刻的是死亡细胞。这一类型给我的感觉就是动作与节奏，以及随机性。最近玩了一下Aura of Worlds,同样是一款非常不错的精品游戏。 [h1]优秀的画面[/h1] 像素游戏特别是肉鸽或者银河恶魔城类型在地图的精美程度上大多数并不会很用心，往往只是起到了一个能用就行的作用。在我玩过的游戏中除了那些剧情向的像素游戏，画面非常精美给我留下了深刻印象的游戏并不是太多。Aura of Worlds虽然说是像素风格但是地图反而却不像其他游戏那么精致，给我一种干净整洁的感觉，还是挺有风格的。 [h1]动作[/h1] 其实本作的动作相比之下并不算多优秀，但是本作的乐趣之处在于包括野怪的动作也是这样，有些滑稽搞怪。这就让我们下意识忽略了其不足之处。游戏的动作性虽然赶不上顶级游戏，但是也不算差，基本的连贯性还是有的。动作与画面整体上的感觉就是复古，是一个颇有年代感的新游戏。 [h1]随机性[/h1] 每一次开始我们都会使用不同的武器，如果像使用特定的武器可以在工匠处进行购买，但是只限于这一回合。目前的武器有弓、剑、大锤等等以及各种副武器类似于盾牌、回旋镖等等。最多可以同时装备三个武器，同时当血量低到一定程度会自动使用药瓶不用太担心手忙脚乱。根据我们走的路线不同，我们遇到的boss也不太一样，只有打过boss才能开启下一章地图。 在地图中会遇到一些随机性物品以及强化武器的锻造炉来提高战斗力。 [h1]整体体验[/h1] 氛围稍微有点压抑，但是还是挺快乐的，虽然各种功能以及体验并不是那么的顶级但还是做到了尽善尽美，个中乐趣还是挺容易感受到的。 [h1]结语[/h1] Aura of Worlds是一款复古的像素肉鸽游戏，目前汉化正在测试中，部分内容没有汉化，整体质量不错，玩起来还是挺快乐的。 [quote]漫话漫谈，期待关注:[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/44551694/]写生漫话家[/url] ←节约宝贵时间，阅读省流测评~ 欢迎加入漫话家的大家庭:[url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/14030826]写生漫话家[/url]←共同探讨游戏中的精彩片段，向玩家展现第九艺术的魅力~ 感谢你的阅读，觉得还行的话，希望点个赞~[/quote]

Was looking forward to this game but was pretty disappointed. Has some things going for it, but for a 2d roguelike, it has a lot of issues in design decisions and mechanics. The game looks fine, and levels are technically procedural gen although all the ones of the same zone all feel the exact same with the same enemies and traps just slightly different layouts. There are a good amount of weapons to choose from. That's about all i can say positive. The roguelike aspects are pretty poor. You use coins only gained from leveling up from XP to buy new weapons and abilities, and a few other small things like more potions, and thats about it. Theres very little incentive to keep leveling because theres no power creep. You can't level up health, damage, mana, armor, or anything making you better. Yes you can buy 1-2 more potions but thats about it. You mostly are buying different weapons to try out which are mostly lateral moves. So you won't necessarily survive longer to grind more xp. This takes away some of the best part. Also the fact you only get 3 coins after an xp level that can take like 30 min-1 hr of playing. But things cost 4-9 coins, meaning 2-3 hours to buy a single item, which is just insane, especially because it may not even make you stronger. This is pretty dumb decision and takes away the best part of a roguelite. Then they add on a second currency items cost, but you can't even get that from playing, you can only get it from BUYING ITEMS, and since some items cost both coins and gems, you will have to spend the coins you grinded for to get gems to then grind more coins to be able to purchase items with the coins and gems. And you get like 1 gem for an unlock and 1 simple unlocks can cost up 5 gems, which is buying 5 items, each of which takes 4-6 coins which is 2 hours of grinding....get the picture? And once again these unlocks won't even make you feel stronger. The gameplay is ok. The levels are too claustrophobic. Theres too many traps and environmental hazards on top of the enemies that while attacking can suddenly decide to ignore damage and hit you. Or guys that can leap half way across the room suddenly and home right in on you without warning. And of course you don't have i-frames when hit by enemies or environment damage, leading to being multi-hit for tons of lost health wasting potions hard to come by. I would constantly be hit by poison or something and wonder "where did that come from". Destroying lights by accidents causes huge damage to you, pots when destroyed leave poison clouds, it just all leads to a lot of cheap damage. The roll is pretty short distance and finnicky. I usually felt when hurt that it wasn't really my fault or I was in control of things because it just all feels a bit janky and imprecise, unlike a game like dead cells. You unlock runes during the game, but you'll have seen them all in the first few hours. Its all random and you have no control over ones you get meaning you don't really build a class. This is also due to the poor starting system where you get 3 random combos of an item and ability, meaning if you unlocked a ton you will have to constantly quit and restart the game to get anything resembling a decent build, instead of, ya know........l...letting you pick your own and not forcing you to waste time for no reason. You also can't see the runes you have unlocked with descriptions for some reason in the pause menu. You unlock some vendors but 1/2 of them are useless. One just gives you different color robes, another gives you a buff that comes along with pretty big debuff (which really isnt that helpful), another has these stupidly expensive pets that once again have no descriptions and theres no real wiki on this game so I have no idea what each of them do or their purpose. The game is just rough around the edges with the combat, cheap level design, no real incentives to grind, a stupidly unncessarily long grind for unlocks, and limited variety between plays. Overall its alright, but I've played many roguelikes that do most or all things better than this game. But its also no terrible. 5.5/10.

Game is good, I like the variety of items, very roguelike. I dislike some maps that we have limited time and we have to rush (I like to play in my own time), but the action is great, very fluid and the game is cute. The dev (and I think he has or had someone working with him) works really hard in this game. Just buy it. Labor of love.

《Aura of Worlds》——在危机重重的地牢中寻找适合自己的玩法，并不断挑战自我。 这是一款极具创意的2d平台肉鸽地牢冒险游戏，在复古像素画风的设计下，隐藏的是一次次对玩家反应和策略能力的考验。玩家不仅要击杀怪物获取金币，并找到更好的装备。同时还要考虑地图中那些隐藏的陷阱和危险，以及规划自己的路线最后战胜boss。 和以往的肉鸽游戏一样，游戏每次结束后都会永久性死亡，身上的装备是带不出来的。同时每一次进入游戏地图都是不一样的。 游戏的玩法就是不断地探索地牢直至集齐五片碎片，每一次进入你都可以选择自己的初始装备以及初始关卡。每一个关卡的层数不同但都有固定的地方。例如每一关内都有一层是陷阱关或者说是竞速关，我们要一直往终点跑，会有致命的陷阱在追我们，同时路上也会有怪物和宝箱。还有就是商店，可以用游戏内获得的金币去购买武器药水或者是道具。最后就来到了boss关卡，战胜boss后我们就可以选择新的关卡，在游戏结束后我们会获得经验经验条满了就会升级，并提供我们1个金币。 游戏的养成系统分为局内和局外。局内的养成系统就是每一次游戏中收集不同的装备，符文等，搭配组合出自己的一套玩法并挑战极限去往更深层次的关卡。 而局外养成系统则是要通过我们经验升级后的金币，我们可以用它去解锁上一局在游戏内拾取到的装备，让它在初始装备中可以带上。同时我们也可以用金币去解锁不同的职业和符文效果，每一次购买都可以获得一个紫色的水晶。用金币和水晶可以去强化我们的属性。 在局外养成系统中有一个十分有特色的设计，游戏一开始是无法使用这些升级系统的，你需要去地牢中用钥匙拯救被困住的NPC，每一个NPC都对应游戏主界面的一项升级。例如购买装备你就要拯救铁匠、解锁符文属性你就要拯救魔法师。这个看似不起眼的小设计恰恰增强了游戏的肉鸽性，同时在前期也能更好的让玩家再一次进入地牢进行挑战，就像是一个目标让人有前进的动力。 游戏的解谜和战斗自由度十分之高，当你面对一个困难时往往不只有一种解决方案。你可以选择传统的战斗，使用手中的武器打败敌人；或是利用环境中的一些工具进行互动，比如随处可见的宝箱，你可以将它捡起来砸向敌人；或是将天花板上悬挂的油灯打爆，溅射出去的火焰也可以伤害到敌人；又或者在黑暗的地图内，我们可以捡起场景中的灯用来照明，同时也可以作为武器将它丢出去。 在战斗系统上，玩家一共可以装备三样武器，一个主要武器和两个辅助工具。这两个辅助工具可以是另一种武器，也可以是技能或是道具。例如你可以在主武器上装备一把长剑，在副武器中装备一把弩箭和炸弹，或是装备一个魔法技能。 游戏中的武器种类十分丰富，你可以用它们组合出几十种玩法和不同的战斗风格，你可以选择近战武器无脑冲锋；或是利用抓钩在天花板上悬吊，用远程武器消耗；再或者是利用地图上的道具打出出其不意的效果。我相信这里总会有适合你的那一个。 在地图设计上，游戏内有12多种独特的关卡主题和6大主要世界，每个世界都充满独特的陷阱、强大敌人和狡猾的秘密。还有上百种不同的怪物等待我们去挑战。 总的来说，这是一个极具特色和创意的2d平台肉鸽游戏，非常值得一玩。 [quote]欢迎关注鉴赏家: [url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/DCYXJLB] 大川游戏俱乐部 [/url] 欢迎加入Steam组:[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45300930] 大川游戏俱乐部 [/url] 来一起感受游戏的乐趣喜欢这篇评论，也是可以顺手点个赞哟[/quote]

Kind of clunky and overall unsatisfying. There's a reason only ~20% of players have the achievement for beating the first level and only ~8% have the achievement for beating both bosses of the first level. Your weaponry is really limited with mediocre damage and doesn't stun enemies for hardly any time at all while they get to fling themselves across the map as much as they want. The devs have said this is to encourage environmental effects and improv, except there's not enough environmental stuff to reliably do that. Like there's maybe 2 or 3 things in any given arena and they're all either super heavy or break in a single use or weapon swing. This goes for the multi wave gauntlet rooms as well, if you're going to have that either make the environmental objects respawn along with the waves or make the weapons actually good. Meta progression is kind of lame too, the currency is slow to gain and there's a double unlock mechanic where you have to buy things in order to get currency to buy things, but the things that use the second currency also need some of the first currency. And none of it feels very impactful, it's largely just extra charges on specific items or extra random starting accessories/consumables. The roguelike genre is just too saturated with great games for me to put any more effort into this one.

Some games overwhelm you with complexity. this game does the opposite and that’s exactly why it shines. This chaotic, creativity driven rogue lite platformer drops you into unpredictable, ever changing labyrinths where every run feels fresh, every decision matters, and every ability can turn the tide in your favor. Whether you're blasting through obstacles, grappling across danger, dashing past traps, or cleverly using the environment to outsmart powerful guardians, the game constantly rewards smart and creative play. What truly makes the game special is how effortlessly it pulls you in. The concept is simple, the mechanics are clean and easy to understand, and within minutes you feel completely in control. Yet beneath that simplicity lies surprising depth and variety. Each world introduces new twists, challenges, and opportunities that keep the experience exciting and far from repetitive. The visuals may be straightforward and lightweight, but they perfectly suit the fast paced action and ensure smooth performance on almost any system. Combined with its addictive gameplay, a game that’s easy to start, hard to put down, and absolutely worth your time.

[quote]Follow my Curator page, [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/41363546-Fruit-N-Doggie-Reviews/]Fruit N Doggie Reviews,[/url] so you can be updated whenever I post a new review.[/quote] [h1]Overall Rating - Seriously Flawed ★★☆☆☆[/h1] [h1]First Impressions[/h1] I recently purchased a bundle of games, and Aura of Worlds (AW) was a title that I wasn't wholly sure about. Roguelites can be very hit or miss for me, and for some reason, I don't seem to have the best experience with cave-diving ones. Due to how this game works, it's one I could probably beat with enough time and attempts, but I don't have enough interest to do that. [h1]Gameplay[/h1] According to the store page, AW includes procedurally generated worlds. However, it doesn't necessarily change things as much as I'd expect. For example, the third level of Grotto of Guidance always has you fleeing from poisonous gas. The enemies and hazards aren't laid out exactly the same, but I swear the descending zig-zag pattern doesn't have much variance to it. Even though the other stages in any area can vary to a larger extent than this, coming across so similar a set-up per attempt makes it feel stale pretty quickly. In this roguelite, as long as you kill some enemies and gather some loot, you'll earn experience and level up. I'm fairly positive these level-ups don't increase your stats, but they provide different kinds of currency you can use to purchase upgrades or items, such as new equipment, and being able to start in a new area. The player determines what weapons, abilities, or starting gear gets buffed when you make an attempt to obtain an artifact. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3700441699 [h1]Controls[/h1] A simple issue I have with this game is how the controls are set up for a controller. You don't have to aim which way you swing or fire your weapon, but it can be beneficial, especially when using long-range attacks. There's also the option to switch between weapons and items in your inventory, but even outside of combat, I find it awkward to handle. I feel like this game was designed around a mouse and keyboard, as evidenced by the ability to attack lanterns in order to burn enemies. However, using a controller, I find it way too easy to set myself on fire, making that a liability, instead of a trap to spring on foes. [h1]Story[/h1] From making trips into the caves, you'll occasionally come across a doorway with someone locked in a cell. If you can find the nearby key and return, they'll be freed, becoming part of your starting base. There may only be a small handful of these NPCs, because I seemed to stop finding them after saving four people. Even though this would seemingly advance the story, their only purpose is to expand your resources. I thought this title would have more lore or plot from the initial screen, but that's seemingly not the case. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3700440587 [h1]Visuals[/h1] Although I'm not an artist, I find the visuals in AW a bit lackluster. It's not even that enemies have generic designs, such as slimes, skeletons, and bats, but their artwork isn't very detailed or crisp. They're also shared across different areas, meaning you'll see them often during your playtime. Due to the pixelation, they look a touch blurry, and don't stand out compared to what you'd find in any random game. Also, when a skeleton archer was firing at me, I was taking burn damage. Since I was actively invested in the run, I couldn't discern specific details, but I don't know that there's anything about its design, or its weapon, that would indicate I'd get lit on fire by those arrows. If so, it wasn't something glaringly obvious in the heat of the moment. [h1]Sound Design[/h1] Each unique location has a distinct song attached to it, which makes sense as they do change the environment enough to warrant a different tune. The songs are tolerable, but there's nothing distinct or particularly noteworthy about them. If I was listening to one of them now, I couldn't be positive it actually came from this game or not. Conversely, despite some annoying enemies and mechanics, at least there weren't any ear-grating noises to drag down the experience. With each area having the look of an abandoned civilization, including structures that make me think of temples, more plot-points could have developed the idea of what occurred before they all fell into ruin. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3700441175 [h1]Pros[/h1] 🌟 Since each level up gives currency, it's up to the player to decide what they want to upgrade. I like this sense of control and freedom. 🌟 You can alter the difficulty before each run. [h1]Cons[/h1] ❌ Before you've made much progress, there's already gimmicks to increase the difficulty, such as a wall of poison chasing you downward. I don't think it makes much sense to include something like that in the first area. ❌ Quite a few enemies attack from a distance, so unless you have a good projectile, you're forced to engage them up close. ❌ Once you obtain an artifact from defeating an area boss, I don't think there's any reason to return there. [h1]Tips[/h1] 🔍 Whenever you open a chest, pick it up and use it as a projectile against the next enemy you encounter. It does so much damage safely that it'd be a waste not to use it. 🔍 Unless you find a great weapon, you don't do that much damage to bosses, meaning survival is your greatest priority. Bosses only seem to have a small range of attacks available. [h1]Final Thoughts[/h1] Simply enough, my biggest issue with AW is how it controls, as I don't find the platforming and combat satisfying or easy to work with. Not only does it feel awkward to platform as my character, especially when trying to fight or manage my inventory, but even how enemies move seems a touch unusual. For example, enemies that leap at you slide across the ground, having a sense of momentum that you have to adapt around when they approach. When your best way of dealing with enemies is picking up empty boxes or chests and blindly hurling them at everything in front of you, it makes using a weapon feel like the chump's choice. Others have given AW a solid review, but only 23% of players actually beat the first boss too, so I'm not really sure what to make of that combination. With so many other options available, I'll spend my time elsewhere. the game delivers a highly creative and mechanic-rich roguelike experience with fast-paced combat, strong build variety, and a world full of interactive possibilities. The combination of randomized weapons, environmental interactions, hidden content, and flexible playstyles makes each run feel unique and engaging. The combat system encourages quick reactions and experimentation, while the progression and equipment systems provide strong long-term replay value. However, the experience can sometimes become visually overwhelming during intense combat encounters. With enemies, projectiles, and environmental effects overlapping heavily, it can be difficult to track what is happening or understand why damage was taken. The tutorial also needs to better explain the game’s deeper mechanics, as new players may struggle with the large number of systems and interactions. In addition, the difficulty curve feels inconsistent, with some runs being significantly easier or harder than others. Despite these issues, the game stands out for its creativity, gameplay depth, and highly interactive world, giving it strong potential within the roguelike genre.
